report.finding: This is Robertson's classic stiff test problem (k2=3e7 makes the B+B->C+B reaction rate extremely fast compared to the others). The model and parameters are correct - this is exactly the standard stiff benchmark, deliberately constructed to break non-stiff integrators. CVODE was configured with `integrator.stiff = False`, i.e. running the Adams (non-stiff) method. For a stiff system that method needs a huge number of tiny internal steps to keep up with the fast time constant, so it runs into CV_TOO_MUCH_WORK long before reaching tout. Raising maximum_num_steps doesn't fix this because the underlying step-size restriction is a stability limit of the non-stiff method, not just an iteration-count cap - it just delays the failure by letting it take more (still ultimately insufficient) steps.
report.evidence: With `rr.integrator.stiff = False` (the session default), `rr.simulate(0, 4e10, 1000)` throws `CV_TOO_MUCH_WORK` (mxstep=20000) exactly as the user reports, even though the same call to shorter end times (e.g. 400) succeeds. Setting `rr.integrator.setValue('stiff', True)` and re-running the identical `rr.simulate(0, 4e10, 1000)` call completes without error, giving a clean approach to steady state ([A,B,C] -> [5.2e-8, 2.1e-13, 1.0]), with no change to maximum_num_steps needed.

changes.what: Switched CVODE from the non-stiff (Adams) method to the stiff (BDF) method
